Three automation agencies to evaluate by workflow

The right agency depends on what happens when a case falls outside the happy path. An unanswered supplier request, a document exception and a backlog shared by several departments need different kinds of delivery experience.

We chose these examples for the specific work documented in a client case or product guide. Client outcomes are provider-reported.

  1. WeAreBrain · Dispatch and supplier responses

    WeAreBrain’s Truck Tyre Assist case describes supplier notifications, acceptance handling and status updates in an ERP workflow. In a trial, ask two suppliers to respond to one case. Check that a dispatcher can see who accepted it and what happens to the second response.

    Read the source from WeAreBrain

  2. Slalom · Customer support operations

    Slalom’s Genie case identifies the client, the support function and a rollout involving 180 agents and supervisors. Ask the delivery lead which parts of a comparable bid cover training, queue configuration and post-launch support. Price those separately so a cheaper prototype is easy to spot alongside a fully staffed rollout.

    Read the source from Slalom

  3. Capgemini · Automation across several departments

    The ZF case documents Capgemini’s work on a global automation service. For a buyer with several candidate workflows, the first deliverable could be a prioritized backlog. Ask each process owner to identify the exception that consumes the most time, then check whether the proposed pilot includes it.

    Read the source from Capgemini

What to ask before you buy

  1. Bring five anonymized examples, including a duplicate and an incomplete request.
  2. Ask to see the audit trail for one completed run and one failed run.
  3. Before handover, have your operator replay a failed job and confirm that it creates only one downstream record.

Directory

Compare agency proposals on one unit of work, such as a dispatched case or an approved order. Count failed attempts, manual review and maintenance when testing the agency’s saving estimate.

Entries link to provider materials. The guide gives no numerical ratings.

Workflow integration

WeAreBrain

Offers workflow automation and integration. Test two suppliers replying to one dispatch request. Count how many assignments and customer notifications the workflow creates.

Operations workflows

Goodspeed

Describes n8n workflows and AI agents for operations teams. If the quote includes training, ask staff to modify a live-style staging workflow and price their time in the savings calculation.

Low-code delivery

LowCode Agency

Publishes a guide to AI agents that run business processes. Request the cost of adding one approval rule after launch. Include platform usage and any minimum support commitment.

Process automation

Capgemini

Documents the rollout of a global robotic process automation service at ZF. Ask for the cost of monitoring a backlog across two departments when only one of them supplies clean inputs.

Technology integration

IBM Consulting

Offers artificial intelligence consulting. Simulate a downstream outage in the trial and ask who pays for repeated integration calls while the dependency is unavailable.

AI implementation

How to compare prices

Compare the setup fee, support retainer and per-run costs at your normal and peak volumes. Ask whether connector changes and failed-job investigation are included.

A worked example to review

Goodspeed describes a six-week n8n program at Oyster in which employees learned to build workflows from their own jobs. The agency labels the annual dollar impact as projected. Ask a bidder to show the original time sample, the number of completed runs and the maintenance hours behind a similar forecast.

Read the provider’s example

Which process should we automate first?

Pick a repeated task with clear inputs, a measurable completion event and an operator who can review exceptions. A reversible workflow gives you room to tune the system.
